title: RouteWorkflowResult
description:
The engine's route (its fields at the top level of the JSON) with the
source it ran on and what the service added to the request.

diagnostics.description:
Counts over the whole request (unstable: diagnostics carry no
compatibility promise).

locationMatches.description:
How each of the request's locations snapped onto the road network,
from the leg arriving at it and the leg leaving it.

overlaySets.description: How each overlay set reached the request.

overlayUses.description:
Overlays the route uses: every applied overlay with at least one
route edge, with its set item id and versions when it has them.

overlayWindows.description:
Overlay time windows (`RouteOverlay::valid_from_ms`), when
any overlay has one.

qualifiedAccess.description:
Qualified legal access along every routed leg, in route order (see
`LegResult::qualified_access`).

sar.description: The SAR relaxations the routed legs used, merged; SAR requests only.

segments.description:
One per leg, in order: a routed leg's full single-leg result, or a
direct leg.

DirectRouteLeg.description:
A synthesized straight-line leg, shaped so a caller can merge it beside a
graph-routed segment without special-casing the merge.

distanceM.description: Length of `geometry`, summed over its own vertices.

durationS.description: Estimated traverse time at the profile's off-road speed.

geometry.description: Densified great-circle vertices, origin first and destination last.

maneuver.description: The single maneuver covering the whole leg.

qualifiedAccess.description:
Where the route's legal access is qualified (`destination`,
`permissive`, …), on every route (see `crate::sar`).

sar.description: The SAR relaxations the route used; requests with SAR only.

oneOf.description: Routed and costed exactly as `Wheeled`.

A road vehicle (car, van, truck), costed close to driving time.
Private and destination-only roads only at a route's ends.

A tracked or off-road vehicle on the vehicle network: tracks are
strongly preferred, and speeds are capped (30 km/h on tracks, 42 km/h
on main roads). Private and destination-only roads only at a route's
ends.

An emergency vehicle: wheeled and tracked access, and not confined to
through roads (it may cross private and destination-only roads).

A person walking, costed close to walking time (about 5 km/h), as
Valhalla's pedestrian costing: footways, paths and streets alike.

Travel on foot that keeps to tracks and paths: the same ways as
`OnFoot`, but tracks and paths cost half as much as streets, main roads
are avoided more strongly, and the pace on tracks and paths is faster
(6–6.5 km/h).

RouteAccessQualifier.description: The qualifier of a legal right that is not plain `yes`.

oneOf.description: Access for destination traffic only.
Access the owner tolerates and may withdraw.
Access with a permit.
Access for deliveries.

Private access: vehicles going somewhere on the way (with the owner's
leave), no through traffic.
Access for the customers of a place on the way.

The profile may use a way whose class excludes it by default
(`highway=pedestrian` open to cars): some tag granted it, but the
package does not record which, so the qualifier is unknown.

sarFactor.description:
The SAR relaxation's factor on an edge the profile may not legally
use (1 elsewhere).

searchBudgetExceeded.description:
The visited-edge budget ran out after a route was found: the route is
the best found so far, not proven optimal.

searchOptimalityGapMillicost.description:
With `search_budget_exceeded`, how much dearer than optimal the route
can be, in thousandths of a cost unit (rounded up), by the lower bound
the search stops on: an upper bound for unidirectional searches, with
the exact stop (`WAYFARER_EXACT_STOP`), and with the default
bidirectional stop (the CCH potentials are consistent).

durationS.description: Time on this edge's traversed stretch.

junctionBranchAnglesDeg.description:
Signed angles (degrees, negative to the left) from the approach to each
other edge the profile may take at the junction this edge starts at
(U-turns excluded); empty on a leg's first edge.

junctionDelayS.description:
Time lost at the junction this edge starts at, entering it from the
leg's previous edge (turning, yielding, signals); 0 on a leg's first
edge. A leg's duration is its edges' `duration_s` plus their
`junction_delay_s`.

junctionJoiningAnglesDeg.description:
Signed angles (degrees) from the arrival of each other edge the profile
may use into that junction to this edge's departure.

RouteLane.description: One lane of the road approaching a maneuver's junction.

indications.description:
The lane's marked directions, in tag order; `none` for an unmarked
lane. Marks the engine does not know are left out.

valid.description: Whether the lane serves the maneuver.

RouteLaneIndication.description: A direction marked on a lane (an OSM `turn:lanes` value).

oneOf.description: No marking (`none` or an empty value): usually straight on.

RouteLocationMatch.description:
Correlation evidence for a stop from both adjacent routed legs.

Keeping both sides avoids the old direct-to-routed gap where a waypoint was
considered unsnapped merely because its incoming leg was direct, even though
its outgoing routed leg successfully correlated it.

lanes.description:
The lanes of the road approaching the maneuver's junction, left to
right, from that road's `turn:lanes` tags; empty when it has none or
the maneuver is not at a junction.

legIndex.description: The leg of a multi-leg route this maneuver belongs to.

oneOf.description: Arrival at an intermediate waypoint of a multi-leg route.

RouteOverlayDiagnostics.description:
Counters describing what the overlay pass did to a route, surfaced on the
computed route's diagnostics. Populated by whoever applies the projections.

RouteOverlayPolicy.description:
What an overlay does to the edges it covers.
Inside one request: a block wins over a discount and a slow-go; an
`open` wins over legal closure and over a block whose `valid_from_ms` is
earlier than its own (an absent one is earliest); overlapping discounts
multiply, slow-go factors take the largest, and of several speed
overrides on one edge the slowest stands.

oneOf.description: Blocked.
Dearer: `cost_multiplier` above 1 (default 2), cost only.
A hazard warning on the route; costs are unchanged.

Usable by the request's profile (when `profiles` lists it, or lists
none) whatever its legal access says, at `speed_kph` if given. The
edge must be in the package; endpoints do not snap onto it.

RouteOverlaySetBinding.description: How a set's items reached a workflow (`RouteWorkflowResult::overlay_sets`).

boundItemCount.description: Items applied by their bound edge ids.

boundToPackage.description:
The set's `package.datasetHash` is the routing package's: its edge ids
are used as they stand.

reprojectedItemCount.description: Items applied by projecting their geometry.

skippedItemIds.description: Items with no geometry whose edges are bound to another package.

RouteOverlaySource.description: Where an overlay came from, when it came from an overlay set.

overlayIndex.description:
The overlay's index in the request's overlays (overlay-set items
follow them).

RouteOverlayWindows.description: What the time windows of a request's overlays did.

evaluatedAtMs.description: The time the windows were evaluated at (UTC ms).

inactiveOverlayItems.description: Overlays outside their window, by label: not applied.

overlayWindowEndsWithinRoute.description:
Applied overlays whose window ends before the estimated arrival
(evaluation time plus the route's duration). The search is static: it
does not see an item expire en route.

sar.description: The effective SAR surcharges; requests with SAR only.

RouteQualifiedAccess.description:
One stretch of a route whose legal access is qualified
(`LegResult::qualified_access`, on every route).

conditional.description:
Whether the qualifier holds only under a condition (a conditional
tag), at the time the request was evaluated or not.

edgeIds.description: Consecutive route edges of one way with this qualifier.

legalTag.description:
The tag that qualifies the access, as the package records it
(`access=permissive`, `motor_vehicle:conditional=delivery @ …`); for
`destination` without a recorded `access=destination` it is
`destination` (the key is not recorded), for `unrecorded` the way's
class (`highway=pedestrian`).

RouteSarPolicy.description: The effective SAR surcharges of a request (`RoutePolicySummary::sar`).

barrierGateS.description: R4: a gate's and a locked gate's time.

legalAccessValues.description: R1: the access values it opens and its factor.

vehicleOnPathsClasses.description:
R5: the path classes it opens, its factor, the least known width and
whether unknown widths are allowed.

wrongWayFactor.description: R2: its factor and entry time.

RouteSarReport.description: What a route did under SAR (`LegResult::sar`, SAR requests only).

totals.description: Per relaxation used: how often, how far, and the cost it added.

uses.description:
Every place the route uses a relaxation, in route order. An operator
must see these before driving.

RouteSarUse.description: One use of a relaxation on a route.

addedCostS.description:
Cost the relaxation added (seconds): the R3 penalty, or for R7 the
leg's time at the off-road pace (which the route's own cost and
duration leave out).

edgeIds.description:
The route edges involved: for `turn_restrictions` the restriction's
whole sequence (from, via…, to), for `conditional` the closed edge(s),
empty for `off_network`.

geometry.description: For `off_network`: the requested point and the road point it joins.

legalTag.description:
The rule broken: `restriction=simple` / `restriction=complex`, the
conditional tag, or `off_network`.

startFraction.description: The traversed piece of the first and last edge.

oneOf.description:
The leg starts away from where the previous leg ended (the waypoint
snapped to different places for its two legs).

waypointGapCount.description:
Waypoints whose outgoing leg starts away from where the incoming one
ended (each such leg's first shape segment is flagged `WaypointGap`).

elevationModelVersion.description: Identifies the elevation/cost model already folded into range costs.

RoutingSourceId.description:
Stable identity used by the host to refer to a route source.

It is intentionally unrelated to package ids. An application embedding the
engine can use any stable namespace it owns.

SarRelaxationKind.description: One SAR relaxation, by its request name.

oneOf.description: R1: vehicle use of ways closed by legal access tags.
R2: driving against a vehicle one-way.
R3: turns banned by turn restrictions.
R4: passing gates and other barriers.
R5: vehicles on footways, paths and cycleways.
R6: ignoring time-limited (conditional) closures.
R7: endpoints away from the road network.

SarUnknownWidth.description: Whether R5 admits paths of unknown width.
